title: Heterogeneous Tier Adjudicator: credit-led routing and graceful model fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement an adjudicator service that routes incoming requests across free/paid/enterprise lanes based on token-credit budgets, regional affinity, and available model variants. The goal is to ensure predictable SLAs for paid/enterprise customers while allowing best-effort serving for free tiers with clear, auditable demotions and fallbacks to cheaper model variants or regions.
acceptance_criteria: Adjudicator accepts request metadata (tenant, plan, region hint, token_estimate) and returns a routing decision within 2ms p95
Decision includes target model variant, region endpoint, admission outcome (accept / degrade / reject) and reason code
Quota ledger integration: debit attempt happens atomically with admission decision such that double-accepts are rare under concurrent bursts
Fallback matrix: if preferred model/region is unavailable or quota insufficient, routing cascades to preconfigured variants (e.g., 7B-quant -> 7B-int8 -> 3B-quant) with documented quality impact
Canary rollout with per-tenant opt-in and circuit breaker if error rate > 5% or latency regressions exceed thresholds
Metrics and alerts for headroom, admission rates by tier, fallback frequency, and business-impacting degradations
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Spec & prototype adjudicator logic as separate microservice (stateless decision + credit-cache) - create design doc and simulation harness
Phase 2: Integrate with Token Credit Service (TCS) for atomic checks and soft reserves; implement optimistic credit windows to reduce RPCs
Phase 3: Model variant registry and fallback matrix config in Console; wire routing table and region cost model
Phase 4: Runtime integration: make serving runtime call adjudicator for admission and attach decision to trace headers
Phase 5: Observability: dashboards for per-plan headroom, fallback counts, per-tenant latency impact; run canary for 2 weeks then ramp
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs: Soft reserves vs strong reservations: soft reserves reduce latency and RPC contention but can temporarily oversubscribe under pathological bursts; we accept small overcommit with detection/auto-throttle
Central adjudicator vs embedded policy: a centralized adjudicator simplifies policy updates and auditing but adds a network hop; we mitigate with local caching and optimistic windows
Fallback depth: limiting to 2-3 variants keeps decision complexity low and reduces quality surprises; teams can configure per-tenant allowed fallbacks
Region spillover for cost vs latency: prefer local region while below headroom threshold; allow configured tolerance to route to lower-cost region if latency penalty < 50ms and headroom is exhausted

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Atomic credit checks become bottleneck under large-scale bursts. Mitigation: introduce optimistic local credit-cache with eventual reconciliation and emergency global throttle
Risk: Unexpected model quality regressions after fallback. Mitigation: tie fallback events to evaluation prompt-sets and trigger regression alerting with rollback automation
Risk: Cross-region routing raises egress/cost concerns for customers. Mitigation: expose per-tenant controls and default to local-region unless overridden
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal-only tenants + synthetic traffic for 2 weeks
Beta: invite 5 low-risk customers across tiers with explicit opt-in
Canary: 5% traffic for all paid tenants with feature flag; monitor errors/latency/cost for 1 week
GA: gradual ramp after no critical regressions and SRE sign-off
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: fallback.rate by tenant > 0.5% triggers investigation
Metric: paid_tier_headroom < 10% triggers preemptive scaling of dedicated capacity
Alert: credit_ledger_conflict_rate > 0.1% leads to temporary reject-mode across free lane
